versions.short: The bill would create a Water Project Navigators Program run by the Secretary of the Interior through the Bureau of Reclamation, which would give grants or cooperative agreements to eligible entities such as states, Tribes, local water agencies, and nonprofit conservation groups to fund staff positions that help plan and carry out multi-benefit water projects. These projects are designed to improve water supply and efficiency, protect ecosystems and watersheds, and serve communities in eligible western states, Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico. Priority would go to applicants serving Tribes, disadvantaged and rural communities, and groups with limited resources, and grants would generally last up to three years with possible extensions. Federal funding would cover up to 75 percent of project costs, with possible waivers for certain groups facing financial hardship, and the Secretary would report to Congress within five years on the program's results. The bill would also cap federal spending under the Act at $15,000,000 in any one fiscal year.
